newsitem.title: UK: LME options quiet, volatility holds steady.
newsitem.headline: LME options quiet, volatility holds steady.

text.p: Activity in LME options was low-key this week with volatility largely holding steady, traders said.
Copper volatility dipped early in the week, but was bid higher as interest emerged for nearby upside calls from $2,300 up to $2,450.
One trader said there had been some profit-taking on Friday morning, with some sales of at-the-money (ATM) August dates at 22 percent volatility.
ATM implied volatility for August was quoted at 21.5/24.0 percent, September at 23.5/25.0 percent and October at 22.5/24.0 percent. First quarter 1998 was slightly firmer at 18.5/20.0 percent.
"We're at a stalemate...Copper vols are fairly priced and we won't see much change until something big happens in futures or the market really quiets down and vols are sold," one trader said.
In zinc, the market had seen some residual producer hedging, with miners buying downside puts for end-1997 and throughout 1998 at $1,200, $1,250 and $1,300 strikes, traders said.
Volatility was up slightly and some players attempted to lock in gains at these levels.
"The vols are starting to sound a bit high, so some people are selling, profit-taking," a trader said, adding that September had traded at 26 percent.
Traders had different views of ATM volatility for August, with quotes ranging from bids as low as 22.0 percent to offers up to 26.5 percent. September was mostly quoted around 25.0/27.0 percent.
Aluminium business was relatively quiet, although some commission house buying emerged for ATM material and upside calls at $1,800 and $1,850 for the first quarter of 1998 and 1999.
Another dealer said buying of upside calls which had been seen in recent weeks had petered out earlier in the week and some of the buyers had turned into sellers.
ATM volatility was flat, with August at 15.5/17.5 percent, September at 16.5/18.25 percent and first quarter 1998 at 15.75/16.75 percent.
